_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.576919/draftresults?format=json
REDACTION: all identifiers invented. Player names are real NFL players (not
personal data of league members); the numeric player ids attached to them are
PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED and must not be treated as a Yahoo id mapping.
No token, email, real GUID or real league key appears in this directory.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED — THIS IS THE AUCTION-PRICE FIXTURE. The entire file
exists for the three picks at indices 4, 5 and 6, which are the trio that
makes NULL-vs-0 testable:
pick 5  cost "0"      → a genuinely FREE roster spot (a $0 keeper).
Must parse to auction_cost = 0.0, NOT NULL.
pick 6  <no cost key> → Yahoo did not state a price. Must parse to
auction_cost = NULL, NOT 0.0.
pick 7  cost "1"      → a $1 dart throw. Proves 0 and 1 are both real
prices and neither is a sentinel.
If those three ever collapse into each other, every dollar-per-point,
value-over-price and draft-efficiency number computed downstream is wrong,
and nothing raises — the rows still exist and still look plausible. That
silence is why the fixture is here. parse_draft_results() reads cost with
to_float(), which returns None for absent/'' and 0.0 only for a literal zero,
and NEVER defaults.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. draft_results is a COLLECTION: keys "0","1",... plus a sibling "count".
Iterating it as a list yields the strings and no picks; including
"count" as an element yields an int where a dict was expected.
2. The numeric keys are NOT in lexical order here ("10" precedes "2" in a
lexical sort). iter_collection() sorts them NUMERICALLY; if it did not,
pick order — which IS the meaning in a draft — would be scrambled.
3. cost arrives as a STRING for most picks and as a bare INT for pick 1.
Both are real; both must coerce.
4. draft_result carries NO player_id and NO editorial_player_key — only the
season-scoped player_key ('461.p.32671'). player_uid must be
reconstructed as 'nfl.p.32671' using the season-independent game CODE,
never the season's game id, or the same player becomes a new person
every year.
5. There is NO is_keeper field anywhere. Yahoo does not expose one — see
yahoo_draft_keeper.json.
NOT TRUNCATED in structure, but only 10 of a real 12-team auction's ~180
picks are included. Reason: every pick beyond the price trio exercises the
identical code path, and 180 near-identical entries would hide the three that
matter.
